column3: The Hebrew leaves the builder unnamed; BSB supplies Elijah.
The Hebrew places filling the four jars and pouring in this verse; BSB places that speech in the following verse.
The Hebrew begins directly with “Do it a second time”; BSB first includes the preceding instructions about waterpots.
The Hebrew says he filled the trench with water; BSB makes the water itself fill it.
The Hebrew names the offering without “evening” and does not explicitly name an altar approached; BSB supplies both.
The Hebrew has singular “their heart”; BSB uses plural “hearts”.
The Hebrew names the Kishon watercourse; BSB uses “the Kishon Valley”.
The Hebrew explicitly says to go up and repeats going up; BSB leaves the upward direction implicit. It leaves the final speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Elijah.
The Hebrew leaves both speakers unnamed and does not specify a chariot; BSB supplies “the servant”, Elijah, and “your chariot”.
The Hebrew says he girded his loins; BSB specifies tucking his cloak into his belt.
